text:
hannah: Alert from data-loss-detector: found a public ACL on `snapshots-prod/snap-20260301-ef12.tar.gz` in rd-backups-us-west-2. It appears unencrypted (no SSE headers). Marking as incident P1 for triage.
raj: Who performed the upload? Any PutObject events in CloudTrail?
monica: quick paste of S3 metadata and a CloudTrail snippet below. Looks like uploader was `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-uploader` assumed by `service/backup-uploader-agent` (internal). No SSE header in PutObject.
```text
$ aws s3api head-object --bucket rd-backups-us-west-2 --key snapshots-prod/snap-20260301-ef12.tar.gz
{ "ContentLength": 234567890, "ETag": "\"abcd1234\"", "LastModified": "2026-03-01T08:11:22Z" }
```
```json
CloudTrail event (truncated):
{
  "eventTime": "2026-03-01T08:11:21Z",
  "eventName": "PutObject",
  "userIdentity": { "arn": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/backup-uploader/agent-session" },
  "requestParameters": { "bucketName": "rd-backups-us-west-2", "key": "snapshots-prod/snap-20260301-ef12.tar.gz" }
}
```
sec-oncall: Confirming receipt. First actions: (A) lock down the object's ACL & bucket public access, (B) identify scope of unencrypted uploads, (C) revoke any temporary KMS grants that might expose key material, (D) begin forensic snapshot and S3 access logs export.
monica: Lockdown commands:
```bash
# block public ACLs and public policies at bucket level
aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket rd-backups-us-west-2 --public-access-block-configuration '{"BlockPublicAcls":true,"IgnorePublicAcls":true,"BlockPublicPolicy":true,"RestrictPublicBuckets":true}'
# remove any public ACL on the object
aws s3api put-object-acl --bucket rd-backups-us-west-2 --key snapshots-prod/snap-20260301-ef12.tar.gz --acl private
# tag object for incident tracking
aws s3api put-object-tagging --bucket rd-backups-us-west-2 --key snapshots-prod/snap-20260301-ef12.tar.gz --tagging 'TagSet=[{Key=incident,Value=I-20260301-01}]'
```
raj: How many objects might be affected? Query for non-SSE PutObject events in CloudTrail. Quick query: look for PutObject events where requestParameters does NOT include x-amz-server-side-encryption.
forensics-bot: suggested CloudTrail lookup (pseudo):
```sql
SELECT eventTime, userIdentity.arn, requestParameters.bucketName, requestParameters.key
FROM cloudtrail_events
WHERE eventName = 'PutObject' AND (requestParameters.headers NOT LIKE '%x-amz-server-side-encryption%')
  AND requestParameters.bucketName LIKE 'rd-backups-%'
  AND eventTime >= '2026-02-28T00:00:00Z'
ORDER BY eventTime DESC
LIMIT 1000
```
monica: Also check S3 server access logs for any GET requests to the object between 2026-03-01T08:11:21Z and now. If anyone fetched it, we need to know.
sec-oncall: Immediate mitigation: set bucket policy to require SSE-KMS for PUTs and deny any PutObject without x-amz-server-side-encryption header. Example policy snippet to attach to bucket (apply ASAP).
```json
{ "Effect": "Deny", "Principal": "*", "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::rd-backups-us-west-2/*", "Condition": { "StringNotEquals": { "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms" } } }
```
raj: We'll also rotate the CMK used for backups and revoke any grants that are not explicitly required. Steps: identify key ARNs used by backup pipeline (alias/rd-backups), list active grants, retire unneeded grants. Example commands below.
```bash
# list grants
aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/rd-backups
# retire/revoke grant
aws kms retire-grant --key-id alias/rd-backups --grant-id <grant-id>
aws kms revoke-grant --key-id alias/rd-backups --grant-id <grant-id>
# create new key (if rotating) and update pipeline config
aws kms create-key --description "rd-backups rotation 2026-03-01 incident"
```
monica: Evidence: I cross-checked and found 4 PutObject events in the last 72h missing SSE header, all by the same assumed role. Might be a regression in the agent that dropped headers for large multi-part uploads.
sec-oncall: Triage hypotheses: (1) agent bug skipping SSE header on multipart finalization, (2) new IAM policy allowed unauthenticated uploads or misconfigured resource-based policy, (3) an attacker used valid credentials to upload unencrypted data. We need to prioritize (1) and (3).
forensics-bot: Recommended steps: snapshot S3 bucket (inventory all keys + metadata), export CloudTrail and S3 access logs to a locked forensic bucket (different account), collect EBS snapshots for uploader instance, capture process timeline from agent hosts, preserve all relevant IAM role sessions and STS tokens listings.
hannah: Legal & compliance notified. We may have to notify customers if any object was publicly accessible and downloaded. Need to know scope (downloads) before drafting customer comms.
raj: Immediate changes I'm pushing: 1) apply the Deny PutObject unless SSE-KMS policy to bucket (non-disruptive for properly configured agents), 2) enforce S3 Block Public Access across all backup buckets via automation, 3) add an IAM condition to backup-uploader role disallowing s3:PutObjectAcl=public-read, 4) create a short-lived feature flag to force uploads through the staging proxy which injects SSE headers for in-flight correction.
monica: I'll open a bug against the backup-agent: suspected multipart client not adding header during CompleteMultipartUpload. Will add tests for SSE header presence in multipart flows.
sec-oncall: Detection rule additions: CloudWatch metric filter for PutObject without SSE for backup buckets; alert and page if >0 in 10m. Also search for s3:GetObject events on affected keys to determine exfil.
forensics-bot: Exfil query (pseudo-SQL):
```sql
SELECT eventTime, sourceIPAddress, userIdentity.arn, eventName
FROM cloudtrail_events
WHERE eventName = 'GetObject' AND requestParameters.key LIKE 'snapshots-prod/%' AND eventTime >= '2026-03-01T00:00:00Z'
ORDER BY eventTime DESC
```
hannah: Owners: monica -> fix agent + test; raj -> immediate infra lockdown & KMS grant revocation; sec-oncall -> forensic export, legal liaison, customer comms draft; forensics-bot -> run the log export and produce a CSV of candidate unencrypted objects.
monica: ETA for patch: 3h to produce a hotfix build and smoke test in staging. If that passes, we'll roll to prod under maintenance window.
raj: I'll coordinate key rotation plan if needed; waiting for forensics output to see whether to rotate or just revoke/open new CMK.
sec-oncall: Post-incident: full postmortem, add automated pre-commit test that fails if any PutObject call in pipeline lacks SSE header, and require S3 bucket policies to enforce SSE-KMS. Also add RBAC hardening to disallow public ACLs on backup roles.
hannah: Thanks team. Please post updates and attach logs to I-20260301-01. Paging sec-oncall and forensics for any questions.
